1.assumed: Velocity is the gradient of a displacement–time graph; steepest part means greatest velocity.

2.assumed: A definition in words must use quantities (energy, charge), not units like seconds or amperes.

4.assumed: In a collision the momentum lost by one body is gained by the other.

6.assumed: Series lamps share the same current, so p.d. is proportional to power.

7.assumed: Total resistance includes internal resistance; I = ε/(R + r); then V = IR for one resistor.

8.assumed: Percentage uncertainties add; a squared quantity doubles its percentage uncertainty.

10.assumed: Distance is area under the v–t graph; stopping distance = thinking + braking distance.

11.assumed: Resultant force equals rate of change of momentum, in units kg m s⁻².

12.assumed: Stress = weight/area; area from πr² using radius half the diameter, mm to m.

13.assumed: Light frees more charge carriers, increasing number density and so lowering resistance.

14.assumed: An electron accelerated through V volts gains V eV, so energy per electron gives the p.d.

15.assumed: Impulse FΔt changes momentum; opposing force can reverse the direction of momentum.

16.assumed: Q = It; number of electrons = Q/e; order of magnitude.

18.assumed: Coherent sources have a constant phase difference.

19.assumed: Closed end node, open end antinode; read the fraction of a wavelength shown in the tube.

20.assumed: Express joules in base units via J = N m and N = kg m s⁻².

22(a).assumed: In equilibrium the spring tensions' resultant balances the weight: equal size, upward.

22(b).assumed: Forces in equilibrium form a closed triangle with arrows following round in one direction.

22(d).assumed: Extension = F/k, then elastic energy = ½kx² or ½Fx.

23(c).assumed: Drag increases with speed, reducing the resultant force and acceleration.
